8.60.150
Abatement by the city.
In the event the nuisance is not abated within the time specified in Sections 8.60.141(A),
8.60.141(B) or8.60.142(D) 8.60.142(C)of this chapter, the city shal1 have the right to enter the
property and abate the nuisance found thereon or authorize a private contractor or other
designated agent todo so.
8.60.160
Costs of abatement; notice of assessment.
A.
Upon completion of abatementby thecity, the city shall complete a statement of
costs.The statement shall include the costs of abatement and any other expenses incurred by the
city, plus an administrative fee in the amount of fifty(50)percent of the abatement costs.
B.
Thecity shall sendwritten noticeofthe city's costsof the abatement to theowner
of the property by certified mail, return receipt requested.
If abatement for junk, trash, or appliances is completed by the city using the city's
sanitation services, the sanitation division is authorized tobill the costs of any such abatement,
plus the administrative fee provided by subsection A.of this section, to the owner of the property
that is the subject of the abatement.
D. If the city engages an independent contractor for abatement of grass, weeds,
snow, or ice, the police compliance department is authorized to bill the costs of the abatement
plus the administrative fee provided by subsection A.of this section, to the owner of the property
thatis the subject of the abatement.
8.60.170
Nuisance files to be maintained.
The Cheyenne police compliance department shall maintain a database record of all
nuisance violations, and the nature of the violations as prescribed by state law and city code.
8.60.180
Collection of costs of abatement; filing of lien.
If an owner or occupant of property towhich a statement of costs has been sent fails to
pay the costs of abatement within thirty (30) days after notification, the city attorney may, upon
the request of the chief of police, file an appropriate lien with the county clerk and ex officio
involved, the amount of the unpaid bill, and a notice that the city claims a lien for its costs of
abatement.Alienfor abatement costs may before closed in accordance with thelaws of thestate
of Wyoming. In addition, the city may pursue any remedies provided by law including
assignment of the claim for costs of abatement to a collection agency.
8.60.200
Emergency abatement.
If a nuisance exists on any property in the city that presents a substantial risk to public
health or safety and if the chief of police compliance director, or designee, makes a
determination that the nuisance must be abated on an emergency basis, the chief of police
compliance director may authorize thenuisance officer to immediately proceed to abate the
nuisance without notice or hearing.The determination of costs shallbe subject to the provisions
of Section 8.60.160 of this chapter. A notice of emergency abatement shall be served thereafter
as soon as is reasonably practicable. The owner or occupant of a property subject to a notice of
emergency abatement may, within ten(10)days from the date of service of the notice of
emergency abatement, file with the city clerk a written request for a hearing in accordance with
Chapter 2.92, Administrative Hearing Procedure. The emergency abatement is not stayed
during the pendency of the Administrative Hearing Procedure.
